query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT A2) FROM district; SELECT * FROM district LIMIT 5;
result: 77 district rows with 77 distinct A2 names; e.g. district 1 = Hl.m. Praha in the Prague region, district 30 = Sokolov in the west Bohemia region
validation_method: read-only cardinality and representative row inspection

query: SELECT A3, COUNT(*) FROM district GROUP BY A3 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;
result: 8 distinct regions over 77 districts: south Moravia 14, central Bohemia 12, north Moravia 11, east Bohemia 11, west Bohemia 10, north Bohemia 10, south Bohemia 8, Prague 1

query: SELECT typeof(A4) FROM district LIMIT 1; SELECT A2, A4 FROM district ORDER BY A4 DESC LIMIT 3; SELECT A2, A4 FROM district ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC LIMIT 3; SELECT MIN(CAST(A4 AS INTEGER)), MAX(CAST(A4 AS INTEGER)) FROM district;
result: A4 is stored with storage class text; text ordering returns Havlickuv Brod 95907, Kolin 95616, Sokolov 94812 whereas numeric ordering returns Hl.m. Praha 1204953, Brno - mesto 387570, Ostrava - mesto 323870; numeric range 42821 to 1204953 with no non-numeric values
validation_method: read-only comparison of text and numeric ordering plus storage class inspection

query: SELECT A2, A11 FROM district ORDER BY A11 DESC LIMIT 3; SELECT MIN(A11), MAX(A11) FROM district;
result: highest average salary levels: Hl.m. Praha 12541, Mlada Boleslav 11277, Plzen - mesto 10787; overall range 8110 to 12541

query: SELECT A2, A12, A13 FROM district ORDER BY A12 DESC LIMIT 3; SELECT SUM(A13>=A12), COUNT(*) FROM district;
result: A12/A13 pairs: Most 7.3 to 9.4, Louny 7.0 to 8.23, Karvina 6.6 to 7.75; A13 is greater than or equal to A12 in 75 of 77 districts, consistent with a 1995 then 1996 time ordering of the two rate columns
validation_method: read-only ordering check across the whole district table

query: SELECT MIN(A15), MAX(A15) FROM district; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM district WHERE A15 > 4000;
result: 1995 crime counts range from 818 to 85677, and 26 of the 77 districts report more than 4000

query: SELECT SUM(A12 IS NULL), SUM(A15 IS NULL) FROM district;
result: A12 holds 1 missing value and A15 holds 1 missing value among 77 districts; A13 and A16 are complete
validation_method: read-only null count per indicator column

query: SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM disp GROUP BY type;
result: OWNER=4500, DISPONENT=869; these are the only two role codes

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM disp d WHERE d.account_id = a.account_id); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT account_id FROM disp WHERE type = 'OWNER' GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT account_id FROM disp GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT type) > 1);
result: no account lacks a disposition (0); no account has more than one owner (0); 869 accounts carry both an owner and a disponent; every client has exactly one disposition

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM disp d JOIN client c USING (client_id) JOIN account a USING (account_id) WHERE d.type = 'OWNER' AND c.district_id <> a.district_id;
result: 409 of the 4500 owned accounts link a client whose residence district differs from the account branch district; the count rises to 494 when all disposition roles are included

query: SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM card GROUP BY type; SELECT disp.type, COUNT(*) FROM card JOIN disp ON disp.disp_id = card.disp_id GROUP BY disp.type;
result: card classes: classic=659, junior=145, gold=88, totalling 892 cards; all 892 cards attach to OWNER dispositions and none to a disponent
validation_method: read-only value distribution and role join
